title: POC weekly sync - throughput optimization
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput benchmark results on NovaPay workload, discuss tuning for continuous batching, set concurrency targets and queueing policy, and agree next steps for extended perf run and data collection for production sizing.
action_items: Connor - run per-shard perf test (3x runs at 5K rps profile) and upload logs to shared bucket - due 2027-03-26
Liam - provide request size distribution and peak concurrency windows (CSV) - due 2027-03-25
Maya - send pilot pricing/seat delta for dedicated baseline & attach runbook - due 2027-03-28
Aisha - coordinate follow-up executive demo for NovaPay infra leadership - due 2027-03-30
next_steps: Redwood to run 2-hour extended throughput benchmark with per-shard KV cache enabled; share perf dashboard and raw traces
Customer to provide production request histogram and prefix reuse rates
Schedule 60-min deep dive to tune batching/concurrency after extended run (week of 2027-03-29)
Redwood SE to propose queueing policy (hard concurrency cap + backlog with dynamic batching) and expected tail latency tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-24
Start: 17:00:00Z
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Aisha (Redwood CSM), Liam (NovaPay Infra), Priya (NovaPay ML Eng), Daniel (NovaPay SRE), Sara (NovaPay Product)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to go over the throughput runs you ran last week and talk tuning for continuous batching and concurrency targets. quick check - is this still the same audience?
[00:08] Liam: yeah Liam here, Priya and Daniel on. Sara's on for product.
[00:12] Priya: hi, thanks.
[00:15] Maya: cool, Connor's gonna run through the numbers then we'll talk queueing policies and next steps.

[00:45] Connor: ok quick context, we ran the three baseline configs you shared: hosted-like single-node profile, dedicated 4xA100 equiv, and our autoscale baseline. the key numbers - sustained throughput at your 512-token average request: hosted 1.2k tokens/sec, dedicated ~4.6k tokens/sec, autoscale peaked at 4.2k with higher variance. note these are token/sec across the cluster, not per-instance.
[01:10] Priya: small note, our production average is closer to 480 tokens but with a long tail of 2.5k tokens for certain flows.
[01:18] Connor: right noted. The continuous batching gain came from grouping short requests; when prefix reuse was high we saw 25-30% token efficiency improvements, but when prefix reuse dropped the benefit went down to ~8-10%.

[02:05] Daniel: can you explain prefix reuse? that's the caching of KV for repeated prefixes?
[02:12] Connor: yeah basically the KV/prefix cache keeps key/value states for repeated prompt prefixes so subsequent calls can skip token compute for shared prefix. it's probabilistic depends on how similar user prompts are. we saw NovaPay's checkout prompts have high reuse in 60% of sessions, which is good.

[03:00] Maya: there's also the queueing tradeoff - if we push concurrency too high to hit throughput targets, tail latency jumps. Connor?
[03:08] Connor: exactly. We looked at two queueing policies: a) no-backlog (hard concurrency cap) which keeps p95 low but sacrifices throughput under burst; b) dynamic backlog with batching window (50-200ms) which improves throughput but p95 can drift up during spikes. For NovaPay's SLA (p95 < 450ms on critical paths) we recommend hybrid: hard cap for critical routes + dynamic batching for non-critical flows.
[03:45] Priya: what's the hard cap you recommend? we saw spikes up to 1.6k concurrent requests during promo windows.
[03:52] Connor: based on the dedicated numbers, a per-shard concurrency cap of ~420 concurrent request contexts maps to your desired p95 <450ms, assuming KV hit-rate >=50% and a batching window of ~80ms. if KV hit-rate drops <30% you'd need to lower cap or add shards.

[05:20] Liam: ok so we might need to add shards during promo windows; what's the autoscale lag? how fast can Redwood scale?
[05:28] Maya: our autoscaler can add capacity in ~2-4 minutes if new nodes are available. we also support warm standby pools for predictable events.

[05:35] Daniel: 2-4 minutes is ok but we can't drop user flows - do you support queue depth smoothing or backpressure to upstream?
[05:42] Connor: yes we support token-level backpressure and a soft reject policy that returns 429 with retry-after; and for critical flows we can set guaranteed concurrency where requests are queued in a short in-memory backlog with jitter to avoid stampeding.

[06:30] Sara: is there a cost delta for using warm standbys vs pure autoscale?
[06:35] Maya: yep warm standby is billed for reserved capacity while idle (reduced rate vs full utilization) — we will send exact delta in pricing doc.

[07:10] Priya: about batching window — you said 80ms; how sensitive are results if we increase to 120ms?
[07:18] Connor: increasing to 120ms generally increases throughput another 6-9% for short-requests heavy workloads but p95 will increase by about 40-60ms in our tests. it's a tunable knob depending on your SLOs.

[08:05] Liam: our biggest concern is the checkout latency - if that spikes it impacts conversion. can we enforce dynamic policies per-route?
[08:12] Maya: yes, you can pin policies per route: critical routes with hard caps + small batching windows, non-critical with larger windows and dynamic backlog. we can set up route-level overrides in the config.

[09:00] Connor: showing the raw traces we captured — p95 breakdown shows majority of latency in token generation for long-tail requests; KV cache reduces ~120ms on average when hit. we attached a link to the run artifacts in the deck (see shared link in chat).
[09:30] Priya: the artifacts had an odd label for model name, it showed 'redwood-3b-quant' but we expected a 7b variant in dedicated run — is that a transcript or labeling error?
[09:40] Connor: good catch, yeah there was a labeling mismatch in the logging pipeline; the run used the 7b quant but logs pointed to default name. we'll correct and re-upload. sorry about that.

[10:20] Daniel: are there any kernel-level optimizations or quantization changes we should be aware of? we run on mixed precision.
[10:28] Connor: we surfaced recommendations: use 4-bit quant for the 7b family for better throughput without big quality regression. also enable fused attention kernels on your GPU flavor; that gave 8-12% improvement in our tests. we'll include specific kernel flags in the runbook.

[11:30] Maya: ok let's talk about the extended run we proposed — you asked for a 2-hour steady-state run at 5k rps profile to capture tail behavior; Connor will run per-shard and include KV metrics and per-route traces.
[11:42] Connor: yes i'll do three 40-minute runs to capture variance and upload the dashboards and raw traces.
[11:50] Priya: we'll share the request size distribution and a sample of prompt prefixes so you can estimate prefix reuse stat more accurately.

[13:00] Liam: one more question on queueing - how do you recommend we set queue depth thresholds for 429 vs backlog?
[13:08] Connor: heuristic we use: soft_reject_threshold = 1.5 * ideal_concurrency, hard_reject = 2.5 * ideal_concurrency. ideal_concurrency = shards * concurrency_per_shard (420 for your profile). But we'll compute these with your exact histogram after you send it.

[14:00] Sara: about security/compliance - we need to ensure logs and traces don't contain PII from prompts, is there a scrub step?
[14:07] Aisha: yes we can enable auto-scrub for prompt contents before retention and we support KMS-managed keys and SOC2 audit logs. we'll attach the security package in the follow-up.

[15:20] Priya: any gotchas with deploying KV cache in private VPC?
[15:27] Connor: in VPC deployments KV cache lives in-memory on inference nodes; for multi-tenant setups we partition by tenant; for private deployments we can configure local persistence and strict access controls. no external calls required.

[16:10] Liam: great, last piece - what do you need from us to finalize production sizing?
[16:16] Maya: the three things: request histogram (by token length), prefix reuse sample, and expected peak concurrency windows (time-of-day). once we have those Connor will produce a recommended shard count and cost estimate.

[17:05] Daniel: ok we'll pull logs and sanitize before sending.
[17:10] Priya: estimated due by Friday.

[17:30] Maya: recap - Connor runs extended perf on Friday PST, Liam/Team sends histograms, Maya sends pricing and runbook. schedule follow-up deep dive week of 2027-03-29. any other questions?
[17:40] Sara: none from product, thanks.
[17:45] Liam: thanks all.
[17:48] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and action items.

End of transcript.
